# census-snowflake-sync

[![CI](https://github.com/example-acme/census-snowflake-sync/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/example-acme/census-snowflake-sync/actions)

Load data from the US Census API into Snowflake tables, on a schedule.

## Installation

```bash
pip install census-snowflake-sync
```

## Usage

```python
from census_snowflake_sync import Pipeline

Pipeline(dataset="acs/acs5", year=2024).sync(table="CENSUS.ACS5")
```

## Features

- Incremental loads with a state table
- Retries with backoff on Census API rate limits
- Schema mapping from Census variables to Snowflake columns
- Works with Airflow, Dagster and plain cron for automation and scheduling

## Configuration

Set SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT, SNOWFLAKE_USER and a key pair. The Census API key is optional for small pulls.

## Testing

Run the tests with pytest. Integration tests need a Snowflake trial account.

# reverse-etl

Sync data between your warehouse and the tools your teams use.

## Install

```bash
go install github.com/example-dataflow/reverse-etl@latest
```

## Quick start

```bash
reverse-etl sync --from snowflake --to salesforce
```

Connectors: Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Census, Salesforce, HubSpot.

A Python client is available for triggering syncs from a pipeline.
